question: Which statement best describes Main property?
options: `box-sizing: border-box` makes a declared width include padding and border. This makes sizing easier to predict. Apply it consistently, including pseudo-elements when needed. A reset can establish this baseline, but the team should understand the rule rather than copy it without context. Border-box makes declared dimensions include padding and border, which reduces arithmetic. It does not decide the layout width or prevent content overflow. Border-box is like measuring the outside of a packed box, not only its contents.

A normalize stylesheet aims to make useful defaults behave more consistently across browsers. It is like adjusting an uneven table rather than removing it. It may suit a project that wants semantic defaults with fewer surprises. Know what it adds before installing another dependency. Normalize files address selected browser differences; they do not guarantee identical rendering. Test supported browsers for the parts of the interface that matter.

A reset removes or changes browser defaults to create a consistent starting point. It can also remove useful spacing or focus appearance. Treat it like clearing a workbench: keep the tools the project needs. Read the reset rules and restore meaningful focus indicators and control behavior. A reset should be small enough to understand. When a control loses a visible state, restore it deliberately instead of adding a broad override.

A user-agent stylesheet is the browser’s built-in set of styles. It supplies defaults for margins, fonts, buttons, and display behavior. These defaults help a page work before custom CSS, but some details vary across browsers. Inspect the defaults before deciding that they are a problem to solve. Default rules provide useful behavior as well as appearance. Compare the built-in style with the design requirement before removing it. Browser defaults are like a starter template supplied with a new notebook.
